<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On 8x MI210 the GPUs form two fully connected 4-GPU XGMI islands joined only by PCIe. The flat custom all-reduce needs every GPU linked to every other, so at TP=8 it turns itself off and every all-reduce goes through RCCL's ring, which crosses PCIe on every step. This PR adds an `ISLAND` backend that reduces inside each island first, then across GPU pairs:

- below 2.25 MiB: the existing custom all-reduce inside each island, then across the GPU pair at the same island position;
- from 2.25 MiB: RCCL reduce-scatter inside the island, all-reduce of the quarter-size shard across the four pairs, all-gather inside the island.

It adds no kernels (it reuses `CustomAllreduce` and `PyNcclCommunicator`), and both paths also run inside CUDA graphs. Fully connected gfx90a groups (MI210 TP=2/4, MI250X TP=8) are handled by #63226; the two PRs don't overlap.

## Claims

- TP=8, Qwen2.5-72B on 8x MI210: decode TPOT −12.5% / −23% / −18% at 1 / 8 / 16 users, TTFT −18% on a 3k-token prompt.
- Only active for that topology on ROCm; everything else keeps its current backend. `VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_ALLREDUCE=0` turns it off.

## Validation

8x MI210 (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7 are the islands), ROCm 7.2, upstream's nightly ROCm image with this PR's files mounted over it.

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct -tp 8 --max-num-seqs 16`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --temperature 0` (128 in / 256 out; prefill 3,000 in / 32 out), four boots per comparison in on-off-off-on order:

| | 1 user | 8 users | 16 users |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode TPOT p50, off → on | 26.7 → 23.3 ms | 53.2 → 41.0 ms | 53.9 → 44.1 ms |

Prefill 3k TTFT p50: 1,099 → 905 ms. With `--max-num-seqs 256`, 192-480-token prompts run the large path inside CUDA graphs and their TTFT drops 7-16%. Greedy outputs of an on boot and an off boot match on 9-12 of 16 prompts, the same rate as two boots of the same arm. No accuracy benchmark was run.

<details>
<summary>Component timings (µs per all-reduce, tokens x 6144 bf16, vs the group's PyNccl)</summary>

| Tokens | Path | Island | PyNccl |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | custom | 37 | 39 |
| 2-8 | custom | 32 | 76-77 |
| 64 | custom | 79 | 101 |
| 128 | custom | 139 | 149 |
| 192 | hierarchical | 145 | 202 |
| 1,024 | hierarchical | 471 | 827 |
| 4,096 | hierarchical | 1,716 | 3,215 |

</details>

Tests: `pytest tests/distributed/test_island_all_reduce.py` gives 13 passed (topology detection without GPUs, sums vs fp32 on both paths in bf16/fp16, islands interleaved in rank order, declined sizes, custom path off, graph replay through `graph_capture()`). `test_custom_all_reduce.py` and `test_pynccl.py` give the same result with and without this PR. With #63226 applied too, TP=8 still selects `ISLAND`. A server with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and speculative decoding (Qwen3-8B + DFlash, both model runners) run cleanly. AMD CI has no MI200, so only the topology test runs there.

## Details

- Islands come from the link topology (`is_fully_connected`), so the TP rank order doesn't have to follow them. Anything else falls through to the existing dispatch.
- Both thresholds are 2.25 MiB (`VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_CUSTOM_MAX_BYTES`, `VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_HIER_MIN_BYTES`): the microbenchmark crossover is near 1 MiB, but 1 MiB made 96-160-token prompts 3-9% slower in a server.
- The custom kernels always copy into the pre-registered buffer: registered graph buffers give wrong sums on MI210 (`test_custom_allreduce[test_target1-2-2]` fails on main; #63226 forces copy-in for the flat path for the same reason).
- With a draft model on the V1 model runner the custom path is off: V1 replays drafter graphs before `graph_capture()` fills in the buffer addresses, which crashed with `hipErrorIllegalAddress`. V2 is unaffected.
- Off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, since the algorithm depends on size.
- Limitations: tested on 8x MI210 with one hidden size (6144). Running the large path alongside GPU-direct RDMA from the same GPUs hard-reset our node, which looks like a platform issue. `--disable-custom-all-reduce` doesn't turn the backend off yet, because vLLM sets it itself on MI200 today; I'll follow up once #63226 lands.

No existing PR or issue covers this; related: #63226, #19744 (QuickReduce), #46065 (AITER all-reduce).

Questions: should it be on by default for this topology or opt-in? Is the GPU-free test plus our MI210 logs enough without MI200 CI?

On question 3, some data from the other MI200 case: a fully connected MI250X node at TP=8, which this PR leaves on RCCL.

We enabled the flat custom all-reduce on gfx90a with copy-in forced under graph capture (`register_graph_buffers=False`), behind an opt-in env var: https://github.com/jbelofamd/vllm/tree/pr/rocm-custom-ar-gfx90a (one commit on main, four files, with a small platform test).

- **Microbenchmark** (T x 4096 bf16, TP8, graph replay): 7.3 us vs 33 us on RCCL at T=4, and 56.8 us vs 158.5 us at T=256. The outputs matched RCCL bit for bit.
- **Registered graph buffers:** we hit what looks like the same problem you describe on MI210. A TP8 x PP6 MoE model gave fluent but wrong answers on 24 of 30 probe prompts, at every capture size we tried.
- **With copy-in:** the same deployment with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs got 30/30 probes right and 0.98 on gsm8k. Throughput per GPU over our load ladder (geometric mean) was 6.91 vs 4.70 with graphs on RCCL, +47%.

The branch only touches the flat path:
- `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()` also returns True on gfx90a when `VLLM_ROCM_CUSTOM_AR_GFX90A=1`.
- `CudaCommunicator` passes `register_graph_buffers=False` on gfx90a.
- AITER all-reduce and QuickReduce keep their CDNA3+ gates.

We don't understand the root cause of the registered-buffer corruption either; we avoid that path rather than fix it. We haven't tried this on MI210.

If reviewers prefer the flat route for single-island / fully connected groups, we're happy to open this as its own PR, or you can fold it into this one, whichever is easier. It wouldn't replace your two-level path for 8x MI210.

Thanks @jbelofamd, this is really useful and matches what we see: registered graph buffers give wrong sums on both gfx90a parts, and copy-in fixes it on both. If it helps to reproduce on a small setup, `test_custom_allreduce[test_target1-2-2]` in `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (CUDA graphs, TP=2 × PP=2, 4 GPUs) fails on our MI210 node, while the TP=2, PP=1 graph case passes.

Your branch and the one-island mode here overlap: for MI210 TP=2/4 both run the flat kernel with copy-in. Your route is simpler, so I'd suggest opening it as its own PR, and I'll drop the one-island mode from this one once yours lands. This PR already steps aside when `use_custom_allreduce()` returns True, so nothing breaks in between. The two-island TP=8 path stays either way.

Two things from our MI210 numbers you may want to consider: at TP=4, RCCL catches up at about 3 MB, below the default 8 MiB limit (this PR caps at 2.25 MiB; see the component table in the description), while at TP=2 the custom kernel stayed ahead of RCCL up to 48 MB in our measurements. And once the one-island mode is gone, MI210 TP=2/4 would only get the speedup if your switch is set, so it may be worth discussing making it default to on for gfx90a now that copy-in is forced.

hi @omar-bahaa !

Thanks very much, that's helpful.  Great comment.

I've split the branch into its own PR: #63226. Following your suggestion, it is now on by default for gfx90a, with VLLM_ROCM_CUSTOM_AR_GFX90A=0 to fall back to RCCL (my earlier comment described it as opt-in). Copy-in under capture is forced on gfx90a as before, and AITER all-reduce and QuickReduce keep their CDNA3+ gates.  Dropping the one-island mode here once it lands sounds right to me; your two-island TP=8 path will stay as is.

Ok so your reproducer on MI250X. test_custom_allreduce[test_target1-2-2] passes on MI250X both with registered buffers (main) and with copy-in.  So does graph_allreduce at TP=2/4/8 x PP=1/2, and so does a bit-exact size sweep (below) on registered buffers at TP=2/4/8.  So on the MI250X I can't reproduce the corruption at the unit level.  Our evidence there is only the model-level one: a TP8 x PP6 MoE model with wrong answ ers on 24/30 prompts with registered buffers, 30/30 with copy-in.  Your MI210 failure is the only unit-level signal we have.  Could you please run test_target1-2-2 with the branch on your MI210 node to confirm copy-in fixes it there?

On the topic of MI210 TP=2 across islands. One thing that default-on now touches: CustomAllreduce skips the fully-connected check when world_size == 2. A TP=2 group that spans the two MI210 islands would therefore get the flat kernel.  I haven't tested this on an MI210.  Does your PR's topology handling already route that case somewhere, or have you measured it?

Here is the size sweep on MI250X that I mentiond above.  I ran custom (copy-in and registered) vs RCCL from 64 KB to 64 MB on one MI250X node (8 GCDs, vLLM main, ROCm 7.14, RCCL 2.30.4), graph-captured, bit-exact against RCCL.  The speedup is RCCL time / copy-in time:


  So your TP=4 observation holds on MI250X too: RCCL catches up between 3 and 4 MiB, right where it changes algorithm. TP=8 stays ahead past 8 MiB, and TP=2
  depends on which pair of GCDs is used. That makes a cap keyed by world size a better fit than one for all of gfx90a: a 2.25 MiB cap everywhere would give

  -the "7.3 us vs 33 us" microbenchmark was on registered buffers.  With copy-in, 64 KB at TP=8 is 16 us vs 34 us on RCCL, about 2x.  Copy-in's extra copy costs 1.3-3.7x the registered time below 1 MB, and 5-25% above 4 MB.
  -the RCCL numbers above have RCCL's scratch kept resident (HSA_SCRATCH_SINGLE_LIMIT=268435456 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1).  With ROCm 7.14's defaults, RCCL on gfx90a pays about 180 us per call: its kernels' scratch is allocated and freed on every dispatch.  vLLM's ROCm base images set HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1, so this mainly hits custom-built images like the one we served from.  Without it, the custom kernel wins up to 64 MB at TP=2, ~16 MB at TP=4 and ~20 MB at TP=8.  The +47% end-to-end number in my earlier comment was measured against RCCL in that default setting, so part of itis that gap.

**Reproducer.** `test_custom_allreduce[test_target1-2-2]` fails 3 of 3 times on main: 0.1-0.2% of elements are wrong, always in blocks of 512, max abs diff 15 on integer inputs. With #63226 it passes 3 of 3, and `tests/platforms/test_rocm_custom_allreduce.py` plus the whole `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` give 66 passed, 1 skipped. So copy-in fixes it on MI210.

**TP=2 across the islands.** You're right that this PR doesn't route it: the two-island path only handles 8 GPUs, and a 2-GPU group that isn't fully connected falls back to the flat kernel with your change. It works there over PCIe, bit-exact against RCCL.

**Caps on MI210.** Custom vs RCCL, graph-captured (speedup = RCCL time / custom time; full numbers below). The cost columns are how much slower the all-reduce gets on the affected sizes with that cap: either the custom kernel runs where RCCL is faster, or RCCL runs where the custom kernel is faster.

| Case | Custom vs RCCL | Best cap on MI210 | Cost with a 2.25 MiB cap | Cost with 4 MiB | Cost with 8 MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=2, one island (GPUs 0,1: XGMI) | ahead at every size: 2.6x at 64 KiB, 1.2x at 2 MiB, 1.07x at 64 MiB | none below 64 MiB | 7-21% on ≥ 2.25 MiB | 7-13% on ≥ 4 MiB | 7-9% on ≥ 8 MiB |
| TP=2, across islands (GPUs 0,4: PCIe) | 1.8x at 64 KiB, 1.1x at 1 MiB, level at 2.25 MiB, then 0.93-0.98x | about 2.25 MiB | about 1% at 2.25 MiB | 2-4% on 2.5-4 MiB | 2-6% on 2.5-8 MiB |
| TP=4, one island (GPUs 0-3) | 4.3x at 64 KiB, 1.35x at 1 MiB, 1.04-1.05x at 2.5-2.75 MiB, 0.97-1.03x at 3-3.5 MiB, 0.93-0.94x from 4 MiB, 0.79x at 64 MiB | about 3 MiB | 3-8% on 2.25-3.25 MiB | 1-3% on 3-3.9 MiB | 1-14% on 3-8 MiB |

So for #63226's caps on MI210 (4 MiB at TP=4 and 8 MiB otherwise):
- TP=4, 4 MiB: costs 1-3%, on 3-3.9 MiB tensors only. 3 MiB fits MI210 best but only saves those 1-3% (and loses 3% at 3.25 MiB somehow), so I'd keep 4 MiB for gfx90a.
- TP=2 in one island, 8 MiB: too low for MI210. The custom kernel is still 7-9% faster than RCCL above 8 MiB (up to 64 MiB, the largest we measured), and those tensors lose that. A higher cap for all of gfx90a would hurt the MI250X GCD pairs that cross near 6 MiB in your sweep, so this would need an MI210-specific value (e.g. keyed on the device name).
- TP=2 across islands, 8 MiB: costs 2-6% on 2.5-8 MiB tensors. A ~2 MiB cap for 2-GPU groups that aren't fully connected would fix it, but it's small; decode sizes gain 1.1-1.8x either way.

detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On 8x MI210 the GPUs form two fully connected 4-GPU XGMI islands joined only by PCIe. The flat custom all-reduce needs every GPU linked to every other, so at TP=8 it turns itself off and every all-reduce goes through RCCL's ring, which crosses PCIe on every step. This PR adds an `ISLAND` backend that reduces inside each island first, then across GPU pairs:

- below 2.25 MiB: the existing custom all-reduce inside each island, then across the GPU pair at the same island position;
- from 2.25 MiB: RCCL reduce-scatter inside the island, all-reduce of the quarter-size shard across the four pairs, all-gather inside the island.

It adds no kernels (it reuses `CustomAllreduce` and `PyNcclCommunicator`), and both paths also run inside CUDA graphs. Fully connected gfx90a groups (MI210 TP=2/4, MI250X TP=8) are handled by #63226; the two PRs don't overlap.

## Claims

- TP=8, Qwen2.5-72B on 8x MI210: decode TPOT −12.5% / −23% / −18% at 1 / 8 / 16 users, TTFT −18% on a 3k-token prompt.
- Only active for that topology on ROCm; everything else keeps its current backend. `VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_ALLREDUCE=0` turns it off.

## Validation

8x MI210 (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7 are the islands), ROCm 7.2, upstream's nightly ROCm image with this PR's files mounted over it.

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct -tp 8 --max-num-seqs 16`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --temperature 0` (128 in / 256 out; prefill 3,000 in / 32 out), four boots per comparison in on-off-off-on order:

| | 1 user | 8 users | 16 users |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode TPOT p50, off → on | 26.7 → 23.3 ms | 53.2 → 41.0 ms | 53.9 → 44.1 ms |

Prefill 3k TTFT p50: 1,099 → 905 ms. With `--max-num-seqs 256`, 192-480-token prompts run the large path inside CUDA graphs and their TTFT drops 7-16%. Greedy outputs of an on boot and an off boot match on 9-12 of 16 prompts, the same rate as two boots of the same arm. No accuracy benchmark was run.

<details>
<summary>Component timings (µs per all-reduce, tokens x 6144 bf16, vs the group's PyNccl)</summary>

| Tokens | Path | Island | PyNccl |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | custom | 37 | 39 |
| 2-8 | custom | 32 | 76-77 |
| 64 | custom | 79 | 101 |
| 128 | custom | 139 | 149 |
| 192 | hierarchical | 145 | 202 |
| 1,024 | hierarchical | 471 | 827 |
| 4,096 | hierarchical | 1,716 | 3,215 |

</details>

Tests: `pytest tests/distributed/test_island_all_reduce.py` gives 13 passed (topology detection without GPUs, sums vs fp32 on both paths in bf16/fp16, islands interleaved in rank order, declined sizes, custom path off, graph replay through `graph_capture()`). `test_custom_all_reduce.py` and `test_pynccl.py` give the same result with and without this PR. With #63226 applied too, TP=8 still selects `ISLAND`. A server with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and speculative decoding (Qwen3-8B + DFlash, both model runners) run cleanly. AMD CI has no MI200, so only the topology test runs there.

## Details

- Islands come from the link topology (`is_fully_connected`), so the TP rank order doesn't have to follow them. Anything else falls through to the existing dispatch.
- Both thresholds are 2.25 MiB (`VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_CUSTOM_MAX_BYTES`, `VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_HIER_MIN_BYTES`): the microbenchmark crossover is near 1 MiB, but 1 MiB made 96-160-token prompts 3-9% slower in a server.
- The custom kernels always copy into the pre-registered buffer: registered graph buffers give wrong sums on MI210 (`test_custom_allreduce[test_target1-2-2]` fails on main; #63226 forces copy-in for the flat path for the same reason).
- With a draft model on the V1 model runner the custom path is off: V1 replays drafter graphs before `graph_capture()` fills in the buffer addresses, which crashed with `hipErrorIllegalAddress`. V2 is unaffected.
- Off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, since the algorithm depends on size.
- Limitations: tested on 8x MI210 with one hidden size (6144). Running the large path alongside GPU-direct RDMA from the same GPUs hard-reset our node, which looks like a platform issue. `--disable-custom-all-reduce` doesn't turn the backend off yet, because vLLM sets it itself on MI200 today; I'll follow up once #63226 lands.

No existing PR or issue covers this; related: #63226, #19744 (QuickReduce), #46065 (AITER all-reduce).

Questions: should it be on by default for this topology or opt-in? Is the GPU-free test plus our MI210 logs enough without MI200 CI?

+NOT_TWO_ISLANDS = 77
+# Rank -> GPU mapping that alternates between the islands of an 8x MI210 node.
+INTERLEAVED_GPUS = [0, 4, 1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7]

+            ([0, 1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6, 7]),

+        (list(range(8)), lambda ids: True, None),

+    assert out is not None

+

+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=WORLD_SIZE,
+    )
+    iar = IslandAllReduce(dist.group.WORLD, device, list(range(WORLD_SIZE)))
+    if iar.disabled:
+        raise SystemExit(NOT_TWO_ISLANDS)

+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+

+def _tp_group_worker(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    """Backend selection, dispatch and graph capture through the TP group."""
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    init_test_distributed_environment(WORLD_SIZE, 1, rank, str(port))
+    iar = get_tp_group().device_communicator.island_ar_comm
+    if iar is None or iar.disabled:
+        raise SystemExit(NOT_TWO_ISLANDS)
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16

+    for tokens in (8, 256):

+
+

+    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+    port = get_open_port()
+    procs = [
+        ctx.Process(target=target, args=(rank, port, *args))
+        for rank in range(WORLD_SIZE)
+    ]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Two-level all-reduce for a TP group spanning two XGMI islands (ROCm).
+
+Targets nodes whose 8 GPUs form two fully connected 4-GPU XGMI islands joined
+only by PCIe (e.g. 8x MI210). There the flat custom all-reduce is unavailable
+(the group is not fully connected) and a flat RCCL ring crosses PCIe twice per
+step. Instead:
+
+* large tensors: RCCL reduce-scatter inside the island, all-reduce
+  of the quarter-size shard across the pairs, all-gather inside the island;
+* smaller tensors: vLLM's custom all-reduce inside each
+  island, then across the GPU pair at the same island position.
+
+The islands are found from the link topology, so the TP ranks need not be
+ordered by island.
+
+The custom kernels always copy the input into the pre-registered IPC buffer,
+also inside CUDA graphs: registered graph buffers return wrong sums on MI210
+with ROCm 7.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+from torch.distributed import ProcessGroup
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config_or_none
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+_ISLAND_WORLD_SIZE = 8
+# Speculative methods that run no draft model, so capture no drafter graphs.
+_NO_DRAFT_MODEL_METHODS = ("ngram", "ngram_gpu", "suffix")
+
+
+def _drafter_replays_graphs_in_capture() -> bool:
+    """Whether a drafter graph can be replayed before graph capture ends.
+
+    The custom kernels' graph buffer addresses are filled in when
+    graph_capture() exits. The V1 model runner runs the drafter inside each
+    target capture, so a drafter graph recorded for one size is replayed while
+    a later size is captured, before its addresses exist.
+    """
+    config = get_current_vllm_config_or_none()
+    spec = config.speculative_config if config is not None else None
+    return (
+        config is not None
+        and spec is not None
+        and spec.method not in _NO_DRAFT_MODEL_METHODS
+        and not config.use_v2_model_runner
+    )
+
+
+def find_two_islands(
+    physical_device_ids: list[int],
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]] | None:
+    """Split the GPUs into two fully connected halves.
+
+    Returns the positions in ``physical_device_ids`` of each half, in
+    ascending order, or None if the GPUs are fully connected or do not split
+    into two equal fully connected groups.
+    """
+    ids = physical_device_ids
+    if len(ids) != _ISLAND_WORLD_SIZE or current_platform.is_fully_connected(ids):
+        return None
+    first = [0] + [
+        i
+        for i in range(1, len(ids))
+        if current_platform.is_fully_connected([ids[0], ids[i]])
+    ]
+    second = [i for i in range(len(ids)) if i not in first]
+    if len(first) != len(second):
+        return None
+    for island in (first, second):
+        if not current_platform.is_fully_connected([ids[i] for i in island]):
+            return None
+    return first, second
+
+
+class IslandAllReduce:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        cpu_group: ProcessGroup,
+        device: torch.device,
+        global_ranks: list[int],
+    ):
+        from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce import (
+            CustomAllreduce,
+        )
+        from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.pynccl import PyNcclCommunicator
+
+        self.disabled = True
+        self.ca_island: CustomAllreduce | None = None
+        self.ca_pair: CustomAllreduce | None = None
+        world_size = dist.get_world_size(cpu_group)
+        # dist.new_group below must be called by every process of the job.
+        if (
+            not current_platform.is_rocm()
+            or world_size != _ISLAND_WORLD_SIZE
+            or world_size != dist.get_world_size()
+        ):
+            return
+
+        assert device.index is not None
+        phys = torch.tensor(
+            [current_platform.visible_device_id_to_physical_device_id(device.index)],
+            dtype=torch.int,
+        )
+        gathered = [torch.zeros_like(phys) for _ in range(world_size)]
+        dist.all_gather(gathered, phys, group=cpu_group)
+        ids = [int(t.item()) for t in gathered]
+        positions = find_two_islands(ids)
+        if positions is None:
+            return
+
+        # A group ranks its members by ascending global rank, so the k-th GPU
+        # of one island pairs with the k-th GPU of the other: the hierarchical
+        # path needs both ends of a pair to hold the same shard.
+        members = [sorted(global_ranks[i] for i in island) for island in positions]
+        islands = [dist.new_group(ranks, backend="gloo") for ranks in members]
+        pairs = [
+            dist.new_group([a, b], backend="gloo")
+            for a, b in zip(members[0], members[1])
+        ]
+        my_rank = global_ranks[dist.get_rank(cpu_group)]
+        side = 0 if my_rank in members[0] else 1
+        island, pair = islands[side], pairs[members[side].index(my_rank)]
+
+        self.max_custom_bytes = envs.VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_CUSTOM_MAX_BYTES
+        self.min_hier_bytes = envs.VLLM_ROCM_ISLAND_AR_HIER_MIN_BYTES
+        # A zero limit turns the custom path off; CustomAllreduce cannot
+        # allocate an empty shared buffer.
+        if self.max_custom_bytes > 0 and _drafter_replays_graphs_in_capture():
+            logger.info_once(
+                "Island all-reduce: custom path off with a speculative draft "
+                "model on the V1 model runner.",
+                scope="global",
+            )
+        elif self.max_custom_bytes > 0:
+            ca_island, ca_pair = (
+                CustomAllreduce(
+                    group,
+                    device,
+                    max_size=self.max_custom_bytes,
+                    max_all_gather_size=self.max_custom_bytes,
+                    max_reduce_scatter_size=self.max_custom_bytes,

+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=WORLD_SIZE,
+    )
+    iar = IslandAllReduce(dist.group.WORLD, device, list(range(WORLD_SIZE)))
+    if iar.disabled:
+        raise SystemExit(NOT_TWO_ISLANDS)
+    dtype = getattr(torch, dtype_name)
+
+    def check(out: torch.Tensor | None, tokens: int) -> None:
+        _check(out, tokens, dtype, 0)
+
+    try:
+        if case == "small":
+            assert iar.ca_island is not None
+            for tokens in (1, 3, 64):
+                check(
+                    iar.all_reduce(_rank_input(rank, tokens, dtype, 0).to(device)),
+                    tokens,
+                )
+        elif case == "large":
+            assert iar.hierarchical
+            for tokens in (256, 1024, 4096):
+                check(
+                    iar.all_reduce(_rank_input(rank, tokens, dtype, 0).to(device)),
+                    tokens,
+                )
+        elif case == "interleaved":
+            # One size per path; the hierarchical one depends on the pairing.
+            assert iar.ca_island is not None and iar.hierarchical
+            for tokens in (3, 256):
+                check(
+                    iar.all_reduce(_rank_input(rank, tokens, dtype, 0).to(device)),
+                    tokens,
+                )
+        elif case == "custom_off":
+            assert iar.ca_island is None and iar.hierarchical
+            check(iar.all_reduce(_rank_input(rank, 256, dtype, 0).to(device)), 256)
+            assert (
+                iar.all_reduce(torch.ones(8, HIDDEN, dtype=dtype, device=device))
+                is None
+            )
+        elif case == "declined":
+            # 8194 bytes: not a 16-byte multiple and below the hierarchical
+            # threshold, so the caller must fall back.
+            odd = torch.ones(4097, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+            assert iar.all_reduce(odd) is None
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(case)
+    finally:
+        iar.destroy()
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def _tp_group_worker(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    """Backend selection, dispatch and graph capture through the TP group."""
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    init_test_distributed_environment(WORLD_SIZE, 1, rank, str(port))
+    iar = get_tp_group().device_communicator.island_ar_comm
+    if iar is None or iar.disabled:
+        raise SystemExit(NOT_TWO_ISLANDS)
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    # One size per path: custom (8 tokens) and hierarchical (256 tokens).
+    for tokens in (8, 256):
+        static = _rank_input(rank, tokens, dtype, 0).to(device)
+        tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(static)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with (
+            graph_capture(device=device) as capture_context,
+            torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture_context.stream),
+        ):
+            graph_out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(static)
+        for seed in range(1, 6):
+            new = _rank_input(rank, tokens, dtype, seed).to(device)
+            static.copy_(new)
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            _check(graph_out, tokens, dtype, seed)
+            # Same kernels in the same order, eager and replayed.
+            assert torch.equal(iar.all_reduce(new), graph_out)
+
+
+def _run_workers(target, *args) -> None:
+    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+    port = get_open_port()
+    procs = [
+        ctx.Process(target=target, args=(rank, port, *args))
+        for rank in range(WORLD_SIZE)
+    ]
+    for proc in procs:
+        proc.start()
+    for proc in procs:
+        proc.join(timeout=300)
+    codes = [proc.exitcode for proc in procs]
+    if all(code == NOT_TWO_ISLANDS for code in codes):
+        pytest.skip("GPUs are not two 4-GPU XGMI islands")
+    assert codes == [0] * WORLD_SIZE, f"worker exit codes: {codes}"
+
+
+requires_8_rocm_gpus = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm() or current_platform.device_count() < WORLD_SIZE,
+    reason="requires 8 ROCm GPUs",
+)
+
+
+@requires_8_rocm_gpus
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype_name", ["bfloat16", "float16"])
+def test_island_all_reduce_small_tensors_match_fp32_sum(dtype_name):
+    _run_workers(_island_worker, "small", dtype_name)
